data.title: Choose the sentence that uses the word correctly.

sections.question: fully
sections.summary: Completely and to the greatest possible degree; without anything missing.

senses.definition: completely and to the greatest possible degree; without anything missing or left out
examples: Please read the instructions fully before starting.

answers.answer: I fully understand the instructions.
I understand fully the instructions.
I full understand the instructions.
I fully understand about the instructions.

sections.question: genuinely
sections.summary: In a real and sincere way; truly and authentically, without pretending.

senses.definition: in a real and sincere way; without pretending or exaggerating; in a way that is authentic and honest
examples: She was genuinely surprised by the good news.

answers.answer: I am genuinely happy for you.
I am genuine happy for you.
I genuinely am happy for you.
I am genuinely happy to you.

sections.question: greatly
sections.summary: To a very large degree; very much; used to intensify the meaning of a verb or adjective.

senses.definition: to a very large degree; very much; used to emphasise how significant or great something is
examples: Your advice greatly helped me make the right decision.

answers.answer: Your help is greatly appreciated.
Your help is great appreciated.
Your help greatly is appreciated.
Your help is greatly appreciated of you.

sections.question: hardly
sections.summary: Almost not at all; only just; to a very small degree.

senses.definition: almost not at all; only just; used to say that something is nearly impossible or nearly not true
examples: I hardly know him — we have only met once.

answers.answer: I hardly slept last night.
I slept hardly last night.
I was hardly to sleep last night.
I hardly slept at last night.

sections.question: highly
sections.summary: To a great degree; very; used especially before adjectives expressing quality or approval.

senses.definition: to a great degree; very; used especially before adjectives that express praise, quality, or a high standard
examples: She is highly respected in her field of research.

answers.answer: This course is highly recommended.
This course is high recommended.
This course highly is recommended.
This course is highly recommended to you to do.

sections.question: maybe
sections.summary: Perhaps; possibly; used when something is uncertain or not yet decided.

senses.definition: used to say that something is possible but not certain; perhaps; also used when making suggestions
examples: Maybe we can go for a walk after lunch.

answers.answer: Maybe we can meet tomorrow.
We can meet maybe tomorrow.
May be we can meet tomorrow.
Maybe to meet tomorrow we can.

sections.question: moderately
sections.summary: To a medium degree; not too much and not too little; within reasonable limits.

senses.definition: to a medium degree; not too much and not too little; at an average or acceptable level
examples: The weather was moderately warm for the time of year.

answers.answer: The hotel is moderately priced.
The hotel is moderate priced.
The hotel moderately is priced.
The hotel is moderately price.

sections.question: perhaps
sections.summary: Used to say that something is possible or might be true, but you are not certain.

senses.definition: used to say that something is possible or might be true, without being certain; also used to make suggestions or requests more polite
examples: Perhaps she missed the bus and will arrive a little late.

answers.answer: Perhaps you should rest for a while.
You should perhaps to rest for a while.
Perhap you should rest for a while.
Perhaps you should rest in a while.

sections.question: possibly
sections.summary: Maybe; perhaps; used to say that something might be true or might happen.

senses.definition: used to say that something might be true or might happen, though it is not certain; also used in polite requests
examples: Could you possibly help me carry these bags?

answers.answer: I can't possibly finish it today.
I can't finish possibly it today.
I can't possible finish it today.
I can't possibly finish it in today.

sections.question: quite
sections.summary: To a moderate or fairly large degree; fairly but not very or extremely.

senses.definition: to a moderate or fairly large degree; not completely but more than a little; used to modify adjectives and adverbs
examples: The film was quite long but very enjoyable.

answers.answer: The exam was quite challenging.
The exam was quiet challenging.
The exam quite was challenging.
The exam was quite of challenging.
